teach_en: The stroke າ is part of three different vowels. Look at what is written before and above the consonant to tell them apart. || ◌າ | aa | the a in 'father' || ເ◌ົາ | ao | the ow in 'now' || ◌ຳ | am | the um in 'hum'
notes: Recap card, not a pronunciation rule (owner 2026-11-09, LESSON_PLAN decision 18): the same stroke appears in V03, V35 and V36, which looks like a contradiction unless it is pointed out. Format: prose, then rows separated by ' || ', each row 'Lao | sounds like | cue' (the app shows them as a table). Sounds are the respellings of V03, V35, V36 (vowels are the same in both transliteration styles); cues repeat the units' teach texts. Wording by agent. R01 is reserved for dead syllables.

teach_en: A syllable like ສະ stops sharply, with a tiny catch in the throat, as in the break in 'uh-oh'.
notes: Rule R01 (dead syllables), first card (owner decision 25: one brief line, no rule to memorise; decision 11: no tone or length wording). Covers only the short-open case met so far (V01 ◌ະ); syllables ending in k, t, p are a later card. 'Catch in the throat' restates the glottal stop in the V01 IPA aʔ and the C26 letters.csv wording. Wording by agent and curriculum review.
